approved: Transparent and Quality Public Appointments Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would replace the current informal system for filling top federal jobs with a legally binding process.
It would create independent panels and a new commissioner to run merit-based selections, with the minister setting job criteria by legislative instrument.
The bill also bans panels from putting forward recent politicians or political staff for roles, consistent with a 2025 review.
Sets up an Independent Selection Panel for each department to handle competitive recruitment.
Requires the minister to publish selection criteria as a legislative instrument.
Forces panels to exclude recent politicians or political staff from shortlists.
Allows appointments only from candidates the panel puts forward.
Creates the Office of the Public Appointments Commissioner to oversee the system.
Sets up a parliamentary committee to check certain integrity appointments.
Federal government departments, ministers, job applicants, and integrity officers would be affected.
